FOUR FOUNDER BUGS ON FOUR SURFACES, and the first one shows a church the wrong amount of money. (1) THE 100x. "In dashboard in all charts about giving/donations instead of 50$ donated it shows 5000$." `useOverviewData` buckets the ledger by `amountCents`, so the giving series IS cents, and it was called `givingSeries` - the one money-bearing field on the tab strip with no unit in its name, while `giving-data.ts` names every dollar figure it produces `goalDollars`/`raisedDollars`/`pledgedDollars`/`paidDollars` for exactly this reason. Three renderers drew it raw: the Overview tab's "Giving & growth" chart, the Giving tab's "Giving over time" chart (the SAME Series object) and the "Giving mix" pie's slice tooltip, whose `dataKey` is `cents`. THE FIX IS AT THE RENDERER AND NOT AT THE SOURCE, and that is this ticket's STOP condition 2 answered rather than dodged: `InsightFeed`'s giving sentence converts the very same series ITSELF and is already correct, pinned by THE-328 at `$1,235` for 123456 cents, so dividing where the series is built would have turned a $50 gift into $0.50 in the one place that never had the bug - the same error inverted. So the series stays in cents end to end, the field is renamed `givingSeriesCents`, and the single conversion happens where a number becomes text, through `formatCents` - the helper written for the AdminAccounting incident that rendered $105,500 as $10,550,000. EVERY MONEY FIGURE ON THE DASHBOARD IS ENUMERATED WITH ITS UNIT in THE-362.money-units: three in CENTS (both trend charts and the mix) and two in DOLLARS (Campaign progress, Pledge fulfilment), and the four other tabs are asserted to carry no money at all. The two dollar widgets are untouched and THE-290's no-regression that they contain no `/ 100` still holds. ONE INLINE CONVERSION IS REPORTED RATHER THAN SWEPT: `InsightFeed`'s `cents / 100`, which is correct, is rounded to whole dollars as deliberate copy, and is pinned - changing it would alter a figure that was already right. (2) STRIPE ON THE GIVING SCREENS. "Hide everything that talks about stripe. In donations, everywhere." THE-350 replaced SENTENCES and left HEADINGS, LABELS and a page subtitle standing, which is most of what a reader takes in - including the `

Stripe Connect

` sitting directly above the very sentence it rewrote. Eight user-facing mentions removed across seven files; the claim in each is unchanged, only the noun. WHAT IS KEPT AND WHY: `StripeConnectPanel`'s four status branches (the processor's name is the operative information when the button sends an admin to Stripe's own onboarding, and THE-256 keeps them byte-for-byte so the panel returns whole - the sweep excludes that region and asserts instead that a church cannot reach it, by RENDERING the shipped component); `billing-processor.ts`'s 'stripe' | 'dodo' union (#499 kept it so a tenant owned by the closed platform account BLOCKS VISIBLY); `/api/stripe/cancel-partnership`, a real route two components post to; and the SaaS-billing and affiliate-payout screens, which are not giving surfaces. The sweep reads USER-FACING TEXT ONLY off a real TypeScript parse - JsxText, prose-bearing JSX attributes and `alert()` strings - because a grep over these files returns dozens of route paths and identifiers and `giving-data.ts` alone would contribute forty comment matches; every needle is assembled from fragments, after #504 shipped one that matched itself. (3) THE LIVESTREAM BUTTON. "The support this message button brings you nowhere." It was `window.open('/?giving=1', '_blank')` - a NEW TAB onto the app root, when `giving-share.ts` says in as many words that `?giving=1` is the IN-APP deep link and "a member already inside the app should stay inside it" - and it landed on HOME whenever `hasGiving` was false, which is the normal case today because card giving is off at the master switch. It now makes the SAME jump Profile's "Give again" makes, to the `partner` tab that renders `PartnerWithUsTab`, and is `undefined` when there is no Give page so the button is not drawn at all - THE-246's shape exactly, for the THE-193 dead end exactly. (4) THE CRM DELETE. "If I delete a user in CRM, it doesn't disappear" and "I tried to delete my own account and nothing happened" are ONE ROOT CAUSE. The list is a MERGE of `contacts` and `users`, and `confirmDelete` aimed at `contacts/` for every row - so for an app member with no contact record the id is a `users` id and the write named a document that has never existed. NOT A REFRESH BUG: the invalidation already reached the list by prefix, and refetching is what put the row back. NOT A PERMISSION BUG: `manageCRM` already gates the screen and a real contact deletes today. AND NO `firestore.rules` CHANGE IS NEEDED - this ticket only PREVENTS writes, it adds no Firestore operation, so THE-362 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere. Self-deletion was NOT guarded at all, silently or otherwise; it is now refused with its own reason, ahead of the account-backed refusal, because the lockout is the serious half. THE MONEY IS NEVER TOUCHED: the receipt in `tenants/{t}/invoices` is the money record, the delete writes exactly one document in `contacts`, and even the GDPR erasure path - a DIFFERENT operation, member-initiated behind `/api/account/delete`, with no admin-facing surface at all - ANONYMISES invoices rather than deleting them. Deleting a contact does leave `contactActivities` rows behind with a dangling `contactId`; that is reported, not cascaded, because adding a multi-document destructive sweep is beyond what these four bugs need. NO npm DEPENDENCY, NO THEME TOKEN AND NO NEW PRIMITIVE was installed; the lockfile is asserted at its exact pinned length. ONE primitive was COMPOSED: `ui/alert` into AdminCRM, which is precisely the follow-up THE-350 named when it rejected the same primitive for itself. Every guard here was verified by MUTATION - render the series as dollars, convert twice, drop `formatCents`, restore a mention on five different screens, unwire the button, shrink it below the floor, drop the invalidation, swallow the rejection, allow self-deletion, drop the accountOnly stamp - and every one failed before being restored.

entries.why: THE-362 OWNS this file's delete path and nothing else in it. `confirmDelete` sent EVERY row of the merged contacts+users list to a delete aimed at `contacts/<row.id>`, so for an app member surfaced from `users` it named a document that has never existed - the row's source was untouched and it came back on the next read, which is the founder's "it doesn't disappear from the table" and, for their own row, "nothing happened". Four changes. (1) TWO REFUSALS, ordered: self first, because an admin's own row is almost always account-backed too and the lockout is the serious half; then a row with no CRM record behind it. Identity is the ACCOUNT, not the row id - an admin who also has a contact surfaces under the CONTACTS id, so the match is the same userId-then-normalised-email link rule the merge itself uses. (2) THE GUARD IS IN `confirmDelete`, not only in the markup: a refusal that lived in JSX alone would be one re-render from being bypassed, and that function is the only thing here that reaches Firestore. The target resolves from `selected` FIRST and FAILS CLOSED, so the render before the list lands cannot open a window in which a self-delete goes through. (3) THE DIALOG IS ONE DEFINITION rendered on both sub-views - the two copies were byte-identical and a guard added to one of them would have refused on the contact card and not in the list, the same argument #482's `subTabBar` already makes. (4) THE SILENT-FAILURE FIX: `setDeleteId(null)` and `setView('list')` moved INSIDE the `try`, so a refused delete no longer closes the dialog and walks back to the list exactly as a successful one did - the screen performed the whole gesture of having deleted somebody while the row sat there. `notifyError` is unchanged. ONE PRIMITIVE IS COMPOSED IN - `ui/alert`, which is exactly what THE-350 said "a follow-up should use" when it rejected the same primitive for itself, and it arrives alone rather than beside a money-ledger write. NO WRITE WAS ADDED OR REMOVED: the file's five write calls are the same set, asserted. #482's disclaimer text, its `keepMounted` fold and the one `subTabBar` are untouched; #503's `amount: null` + `invoiceId` activity shape is untouched; the file is NOT composed, per the closed card. FOLLOW-UP, SAME PR - THE CASCADE. Deleting a contact removed ONE document, and `contactActivities` is a TOP-LEVEL collection keyed by a `contactId` FIELD rather than a subcollection, so Firestore deleted none of it with the parent: every row was left pointing at a document that no longer existed, and a donation row carries an `invoiceId`, so that is a dangling reference beside the money. `confirmDelete` now sweeps the timeline through `DELETE /api/crm/contact-activities` BEFORE deleting the contact, and the ORDER is the whole safety argument: a failure anywhere leaves the CONTACT PRESENT with fewer rows - a state this screen already renders and which pressing Delete again finishes - whereas deleting the contact first would manufacture the orphan on every failure. It cannot be swept from the client at all: rules are not filters, so a `list` constrained only on `contactId` cannot prove `tenantId` and is refused outright, and adding that filter needs a composite index this repo does not deploy. NO firestore.rules CHANGE. The refusals still run FIRST, before any sweep - an admin's own timeline is never destroyed on the way to telling them they cannot delete themselves - and a failed sweep still surfaces through `notifyError` with the dialog OPEN and the contact intact, which is this PR's own silent-failure fix asserted one layer down. The confirmation now says what it removes (the record and its timeline), what it does not (the receipt, so accounting and giving statements do not move), and that it is NOT account erasure, which only the member can do from their own profile.

THE-362 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file. `Contact` gains `accountOnly?: true`, stamped in `userDocToMemberContact` and NOWHERE else, so it is true exactly when a row was built from a `users` doc with no contact behind it. It is the fact the delete path had no way to ask for: a consumer of the merged array could not tell a CRM record from a surfaced app member, and `Contact.account` does not answer it - that says whether the person HOLDS an account, and a folded contact row carries it too while still having a real `contacts` document that deletes correctly. It is `true` or ABSENT, never `false`. NO READ, NO QUERY AND NO FETCH SHAPE MOVED: THE-342's `orderBy(documentId())` clauses, `CRM_FETCH_LIMIT`, the scoping branch, the super-admin gate, the `NO_TENANT_SCOPE_MESSAGE` throw, the members-read rethrow and the merge are byte-identical, and THE-342's guards still measure them. NO EMOJI: THE-342 sweeps the RAW source of this file, so the house markers are deliberately absent and the additions are written in plain emphasis - this ticket's first draft turned that suite red by forgetting it.

THE-362 owns two lines here, both about the UNIT of one series. `data.givingSeries` becomes `data.givingSeriesCents` at both call sites in this file, and the trend series gains `format: formatCents` - the whole of the 100x fix on this tab. The series object is UNCHANGED and is still passed by reference, so THE-290's identity assertion that the Overview and Giving tabs plot the SAME object, not an equal one, still holds. `InsightFeed` keeps receiving it under the name `givingSeries`, which it has always taken it by and already converts correctly - renaming a correct, THE-328-pinned input would be churn. Every KPI card, the funnel, the mix and every empty state on this tab are byte-identical, and the file still carries no inline style, which THE-276's guard caught this ticket breaking once.

THE-362 owns TWO STRINGS in this file and nothing else. The collapsed Payment-setup row read "Stripe Connect - 100% of donations go to your ministry" and the campaign disclaimer read "counts Stripe gifts alone"; both now say "card giving" and "card gifts". THE CLAIM IN EACH IS UNCHANGED - the same set of gifts, said without the processor's brand, on a screen a church reads about its own fundraising. No read, no write, no gate, no endpoint and no control moved: the `PaymentSection` mount is untouched (and still gated once for both screens), the `STRIPE_CONNECT_ENABLED` branch on the campaign-type blurb is untouched, and `hasManualGivingLinks` still decides whether the disclaimer renders at all.

THE-362 owns the `onDonate` prop on the `LivestreamView` mount and nothing else in this file. It was `window.open('/?giving=1', '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` - a new tab onto the SPA root, which `donations/giving-share.ts` explicitly reserves as the IN-APP deep link ("a member already inside the app should stay inside it"), and which `effectiveTopTab` collapses to HOME whenever `hasGiving` is false. That is the normal case today: `hasGiving` needs `hasGivingRails`, and card giving is off at THE-256's master switch, so a church with no saved payment link handed its members a second tab showing the news feed. It now closes the full-screen livestream and selects the `partner` tab in the app the member is already signed into - the identical two-line jump `onGoToPartner` already makes for Profile's "Give again" - and is `undefined` when there is no Give page, so LivestreamView draws no button at all. THE-246 established that `undefined`-not-a-no-op shape for this exact dead end. Nothing else moved: the `?giving=1` deep-link effect, every tab gate, `hasStripeGiving`, `hasGivingRails` and the whole nav derivation are byte-identical.

THE-362 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-361 owned the one before it and THE-360 the one before that. `RULES_PINNERS_NOW` goes 74 -> 75 and this ticket's guard suite joins `RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE` beside THE-361's entry, never over it - the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-362 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere, and that is a FINDING rather than an omission: its STOP condition 4 was "the CRM delete needs a rules change", and it does not. The top-level `contacts` rule already allows delete to a holder of `manageCRM`; the founder's bug was that the CRM list MERGES `contacts` with `users`, so an app member's row is keyed by their `users` id and the delete named a `contacts` document that has never existed. The fix PREVENTS two writes and adds no Firestore operation of any kind, so there is nothing a rule could have expressed, and the rule is ASSERTED as it stands through `rulesDigestFailure()` rather than spelled as a literal - the mistake this register caught #504 making.
